newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude oil market quiet, paper spreads softer.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude oil market quiet, paper spreads softer.

text.p: The North Sea market was quiet on Wednesday with only a cluster of wet and paper deals reported and market direction hard to pin down.

January Brent paper was untraded but assessed around screen levels of $22.50/55 a barrel in the late afternoon. Intermonth spreads softened in line with the weaker market with Feb/March trading down from +55 cents to +51 cents. March/May traded twice at +$1.0.
CFD levels were slightly firmer near month-end with Dec 30-Jan 3 dates heard done at Feb +25 cents.
The wet market provided little direction with two Brent deals done 10 cents wide. A Dec 24-26 cargo traded at Jan +33 cents and another loading a day later was sold at Jan +23 cents.
A Brent trader thought the numbers might reflect date requirements of the purchaser.
The only other wet deal of the day was a Statfjord cargo loading Dec 24-26 done at Dated Brent +36 cents. The sale of a January loader at higher numbers could not be confirmed.
The Wall Street refiner who bought a Brent cargo on Tuesday at a 33 cent premium to January Brent was expected to buy a further cargo.
The trader was seen booking two VLCCs for U.S. Gulf loading Dec 21 and Dec 25.
Sour Mediterranean crude prices were steady, but buyers and sellers disagreed over market direction after two deals at poles apart this week.
A major oil company bought a part Urals cargo at Dated Brent -12.5 cents c+f Augusta while an Italian refiner bought a cargo on the water at Dated -30 cents.
"(One Italian refiner) is talking a very bearish book, but I wouldn't sell a cargo for less than (Dated Brent) minus five," a seller said.
